skill.name: lavish
skill.description: Create interactive HTML artifacts for visual review, annotation, and feedback through the lavish-axi CLI.
skill.summary: Create browser-based review surfaces for plans, diagrams, comparisons, reports, and code changes.
skill.author: kunchenguid

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans. Confirmed risks include unpinned npx execution and public third-party sharing without an explicit consent gate. No prompt injection or malicious reconnaissance was found.

remediation.issue: The workflow repeatedly executes an unpinned package with npx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited lavish-axi version and integrity value, and require confirmation before downloading or executing it.

remediation.issue: The share command publishes artifacts publicly by default without requiring user consent.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit informed consent, check for sensitive data, and make password-protected sharing the default.

remediation.issue: Passwords and bearer tokens can be supplied as command-line arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Accept secrets through protected standard input or environment variables, and warn against command-line secret arguments.

content.value_statement: Complex responses are difficult to review in plain text. Lavish creates interactive HTML artifacts that collect visual annotations and structured feedback.
actual_capabilities: Creates interactive HTML artifacts for plans, comparisons, diagrams, tables, reports, and code changes.
Opens local artifacts in a browser-based review session.
Collects annotations, selected-text comments, queued prompts, and layout repair requests.
Supports Mermaid diagrams that reviewers can edit through embedded Excalidraw surfaces.
Exports portable HTML files with local assets inlined.
Can publish artifacts to a third-party hosting service.
limitations: Requires Node.js, npx, a browser, and access to the lavish-axi package.
Generated artifacts require careful testing for layout, accessibility, and content accuracy.
Public sharing sends artifact content to a third-party service.
Remote assets in exported files still require network access.

use_cases.title: Review Technical Plans
use_cases.description: Present architecture, dependencies, risks, and decisions in an annotated browser artifact.

use_cases.title: Compare Product Options
use_cases.description: Organize alternatives, tradeoffs, and open questions for focused stakeholder feedback.

use_cases.title: Inspect Code Changes
use_cases.description: Show diffs, annotated snippets, and before-and-after behavior in a visual review surface.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Lavish comparison artifact for [options]. Show key differences, benefits, risks, and a clear recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Visualize a Technical Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Lavish plan for [project]. Include scope, milestones, dependencies, risks, decisions, and questions requiring feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Lavish architecture artifact for [system]. Add a Mermaid diagram, component responsibilities, data flows, failure modes, and decision points.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multi-Surface Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Lavish review combining plan, comparison, diagram, and input playbooks for [initiative]. Collect prioritized decisions and actionable annotations.

output_examples.input: Compare three database options for an analytics service.
output_examples.output: A browser artifact presents a decision matrix, operational tradeoffs, cost factors, risks, and annotated recommendation areas.
An interactive architecture review shows the request flow, trust boundaries, component duties, failure modes, and questions for reviewers.
A structured plan displays milestones, interface states, dependencies, risks, and focused controls for stakeholder feedback.

best_practices: Match the artifact design to the subject project and the user's requested visual style.
Keep polling in a tracked foreground process and apply only feedback the user submits.
Confirm user intent and remove sensitive information before any external share.
anti_patterns: Do not publish artifacts to third-party hosting without explicit user approval.
Do not detach polling with untracked shell background processes.
Do not replace requested visual structure with long, unformatted prose.

faq.question: What does Lavish create?
faq.answer: It creates interactive HTML artifacts for visual explanation, review, annotation, and feedback.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does Lavish require a global installation?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow uses npx, but Node.js and package access are required.

faq.question: Can reviewers edit diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. Supported Mermaid diagrams can open as editable Excalidraw whiteboards during a review session.

faq.question: Can artifacts work without the local server?
faq.answer: Yes. Exported artifacts inline local assets, but remote references still require network access.

faq.question: Is external sharing private?
faq.answer: No. Shares are public by default unless password protection is selected, and content is uploaded to a third-party service.
